region: Mount Kenya, Rift Valley, Maasai Mara and Lamu
title: Kenya — Four Thousand Metres to the Swahili Coast
subtitle: Point Lenana on foot, Hell's Gate by bicycle, resident game in the Mara, and a car-free Swahili town
summary: A 15-day route linking the Sirimon–Chogoria trek on Mount Kenya (4,985 m), cycling at Hell's Gate, two nights in the Maasai Mara in the dry season, and Lamu Old Town by air. Outside the 2,500 EUR line at about 3,400 EUR per person.
introduction: Mount Kenya's Sirimon–Chogoria traverse comes first: four nights in huts and camps from moorland to the 4,985 m summit of Point Lenana, then down the Gorges Valley to Lake Ellis. From the highlands the trip drops into the Rift Valley, cycling among zebra at Hell's Gate, then crosses to the Maasai Mara for two nights in a tented camp, where February's dry grass shows resident lions, elephants and buffalo without the July migration crowds. It ends on Lamu, a car-free Swahili town of coral stone and dhows, reached only by air. Three landscapes, three cultures, one chosen sequence of altitude, savanna and ocean.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a self-drive desert and mountain circuit with a rented vehicle; this is a trek-plus-safari-plus-coast route with a driver-guide, a 5,000 m summit and wildlife that Oman cannot offer, but it is costlier and self-drive is not recommended.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: A package Kenya trip is usually Mara plus a beach resort. This one swaps the beach for a UNESCO Swahili town and adds a real summit trek and a bicycle ride in a volcanic gorge, with community-run visits instead of staged villages.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Kenya mixes altitude, wildlife and Swahili culture better than most of the portfolio and is distinct from the Tanzania concept (D48: no Serengeti, Ngorongoro or Kilimanjaro here). Cost is the problem: park fees and flights place it near the top of the portfolio.

duration.note: Day 1 is the evening flight from Paris; day 14 ends with the evening flight home, landing on day 15.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: About 1-26 February 2027 (finish before the long rains in mid-March)
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: December to mid-March is the drier season on Mount Kenya, February is the driest month for the trek and the Mara, and Lamu is hot but dry. Ramadan (about 8 February-9 March) affects Lamu; March brings rain and Eid.

februarySuitability.summary: The driest and clearest month for Mount Kenya, good resident-game viewing in the Mara and little rain at the coast; Lamu falls in Ramadan from about 8 February.

marchSuitability.summary: Good until about the first half of the month, then the long rains begin: wetter trails, muddy Mara tracks and humid, hotter Lamu; Eid al-Fitr is about 9-10 March.

climate.regionNote: Four climate zones: highlands (Nanyuki, Naivasha 1,900-2,100 m), alpine Mount Kenya, the Mara plateau (1,500-2,200 m) and the humid coast. Planning from climate normals; no 2027 forecast is implied.

february.rainfall: Nairobi about 36 mm; Lamu about 4 mm; Mara roughly 60-100 mm in a long-term monthly mean; low on Mount Kenya.
february.notes: Mount Kenya nights are below freezing above about 4,000 m (frost usual); Lamu 31/25 C.

march.rainfall: Nairobi about 75 mm; Lamu about 25 mm; Mara long rains begin in March-April; Mount Kenya long rains from mid-March.
march.notes: Lamu 32/26 C; plan to finish the trek by mid-March.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Point Lenana is accessible without technical climbing from December to mid-March, the drier season; October-December and mid-March-June are wetter.
climate.seaConditions: Indian Ocean calm in February; dhow day trips are possible.
climate.airQuality: Good in the highlands; Nairobi traffic fumes.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Mara resident game year-round (lion, elephant, buffalo, giraffe, rhino); the wildebeest migration is in the Mara roughly July to October.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan 2027
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Lamu is quieter by day; restaurants may close until sunset; modest dress; evenings are lively.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Public holiday; coastal and Lamu celebrations; closures.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: General election campaign
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: France warns of pre-election unrest, mainly later than February-March.

climate.ramadan2027: Expected about 8 February-9 March 2027. Lamu is almost entirely Muslim; Ramadan affects the Lamu leg of the trip. Trek, Hell's Gate and Mara are largely unaffected.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year (6 February 2027) does not affect Kenya.
climate.tourismDemand: February is high season for the Mara (dry months, warm days); fares and camp rates are lower than July-October. Mount Kenya is busiest in January-February and August-September.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: February-March are shoulder months for Europe-Nairobi; February examples 570-670 EUR return; peaks are December and July-August.

geography.summary: Equatorial glaciated volcano, Rift Valley lakes and gorges, savanna plateau and a mangrove-lined coral island, within one 15-day arc.
geography.distinctive: Walking to 4,985 m on the equator, cycling among zebra in a gorge, and sailing a dhow in the same trip.

landscapes.name: Mount Kenya
landscapes.description: Extinct volcano with glaciers on the equator; moorland, giant groundsel and tarns.

landscapes.name: Hell's Gate and Naivasha
landscapes.description: Volcanic cliffs, geothermal vents and a freshwater lake in the Rift Valley.

landscapes.name: Maasai Mara
landscapes.description: Open savanna and acacia with the Mara river.

landscapes.name: Lamu archipelago
landscapes.description: Coral-stone island, mangroves and dunes at Shela.

culture.summary: Swahili Islamic culture in Lamu, Maasai pastoral communities near the Mara, and Kikuyu and Meru farming country around Mount Kenya.

culturalHighlights.name: Lamu Old Town
culturalHighlights.description: Oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement in East Africa, coral-stone houses, carved doors, no cars.

culturalHighlights.name: Community-run Maasai visit
culturalHighlights.description: A guided visit with a community-owned enterprise; pay directly and ask before photographing.

culturalHighlights.name: Dhow culture
culturalHighlights.description: Sail and boat-building tradition on the Lamu channel; day trips by traditional dhow.

culturalHighlights.name: Nairobi food
culturalHighlights.description: Nyama choma, Swahili coastal dishes and street snacks.

adventureHighlights.name: Point Lenana trek (4,985 m)
adventureHighlights.description: Four nights on the mountain, summit at 4,985 m, an ascent profile steeper than recommended for acclimatisation.

adventureHighlights.name: Cycling Hell's Gate
adventureHighlights.description: Bike among zebra and buffalo; a gorge walk with a compulsory local guide.

adventureHighlights.name: Mara game drives
adventureHighlights.description: Dawn drives with a licensed driver-guide; no walking outside the camp perimeters.

signatureExperiences.title: Point Lenana at sunrise, Sirimon to Chogoria
signatureExperiences.description: Four nights on Mount Kenya: moorland, Shipton's Camp beneath the twin peaks, a 03:00 start for the 4,985 m summit, then the Gorges Valley and Lake Ellis.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The highest point reachable on foot in Kenya, crossing the mountain rather than returning on the same trail, in the driest window.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a licensed operator offering a private 5-day Sirimon-Chogoria traverse with guide, cook and porters; ask for an extra acclimatisation night if possible; carry insurance covering 5,000 m.

signatureExperiences.title: Cycling Hell's Gate and Ol Njorowa Gorge
signatureExperiences.description: Bicycle through the park among zebra, then walk the water-cut gorge with a local guide.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the few parks in Kenya where visitors can cycle among wildlife; scenery of volcanic plugs and steam.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hire bicycles and a gorge guide at the gate or via the lakeside lodge; start early to avoid midday heat.

signatureExperiences.title: Resident game in the dry Mara
signatureExperiences.description: Two nights in a tented camp with dawn and late-afternoon game drives for lion, elephant, buffalo and giraffe, and a community-run Maasai visit.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: February is outside the migration, with fewer vehicles and lower fees than July-October, and the grass is short.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Use a driver-guide 4x4 with a mid-range camp near Sekenani or Talek gate; confirm whether the camp is in the reserve or a conservancy.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Camp 260 + reserve fees 174 + vehicle share 112 + community visit 25 (estimates).

signatureExperiences.title: Lamu Old Town and a dhow day
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the car-free UNESCO town, visit the fort and museum, then sail to Shela and the dunes.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A living Swahili Islamic town, not a coastal resort; Ramadan evenings add atmosphere.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Fly to Lamu-Manda airport (never travel by road), stay in the old town, and hire a dhow through the guesthouse.

travelStyle.summary: Trek with a licensed guide, driver-guide for road legs, bicycles in Hell's Gate, domestic flights and a dhow to Lamu.

transport.summary: A driver-guide vehicle covers all road legs; two domestic flights reach Lamu. Matatus and long-distance buses are avoided.

modes.description: Nairobi-Nanyuki, Chogoria-Nairobi, Naivasha, Mara and back.
Nairobi to Lamu-Manda by Jambojet or Safarilink, about 2 h, aggregator fares from about 113 EUR.
Nairobi-Mombasa economy reported at KSh 1,500; not used on this route but an alternative for a coastal extension.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental with an international driving permit is possible but not recommended: carjacking and fake checkpoints, night driving and poor road discipline.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is possible on tarmac but not recommended; use a driver-guide.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Check with the rental company; a licence in Latin script usually needs an international driving permit alongside it.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; none is needed with a driver-guide.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody rides a motorcycle (boda-boda) or scooter without the legal licence; use the driver-guide vehicle, taxis or walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hire a driver-guide with a 4x4 for six vehicle-days and fly to Lamu.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses in towns, huts and camps on the mountain, a tented camp in the Mara and a restored house or guesthouse in Lamu.
types: KWS huts and campsites on Mount Kenya
Mid-range tented camp in the Mara
Lakeside cottage or campsite at Naivasha
Swahili guesthouse in Lamu Old Town

camping.summary: Mountain campsites and huts for four nights; the Mara camp is a staffed tented camp rather than self-pitched camping.

physicalDifficulty.label: strenuous
physicalDifficulty.summary: Five days of walking with a 10 h summit day at 4,985 m and frost at night; other days are easy to moderate (cycling, game drives).

itinerary.summary: Fifteen days: three days of Nairobi and Nanyuki access, five days on Mount Kenya, one day in Hell's Gate, two in the Mara, and two in Lamu, with Nairobi as the hub.

days.title: Overnight flight to Nairobi
activities: Fly Paris CDG to Nairobi JKIA, ideally on a direct evening service
Buy Kenya eTA and mandatory insurance beforehand, carry printed approval
days.practical: Apply for the eTA at least two weeks ahead; passport valid 6 months with 2 blank pages.

days.title: Arrival and drive to the foot of Mount Kenya
activities: Meet the driver-guide at arrivals and drive about 200 km north
Short acclimatisation walk and trek briefing, kit hire check
days.culturalHighlight: Nanyuki, a market and garrison town on the equator
days.geographicalHighlight: Equator line and views of Mount Kenya's glaciers on clear mornings
days.practical: Arrive in daylight only; avoid airport-road carjacking hotspots with a pre-booked transfer; Laikipia curfew zones are in the north and west, not on this road.

days.title: Sirimon Gate to the moorland
activities: Drive to Sirimon Gate (2,650 m), register with KWS
Walk about 9 km through forest and moorland to Old Moses Camp (3,300 m)
days.transport: 4x4 to the gate, then on foot
days.accommodation: Hut or campsite at Old Moses
days.geographicalHighlight: Montane forest to giant heather moorland
days.practical: Take a short afternoon acclimatisation walk; no strenuous climbing above the camp.

days.title: To the foot of the peaks
activities: Walk about 14 km up Mackinder's side valleys to Shipton's Camp (4,200 m)
Spend the afternoon resting and eating; cold night with frost
days.accommodation: Hut or tent at Shipton's Camp
days.geographicalHighlight: Giant groundsel and lobelia moorland beneath Batian and Nelion
days.practical: Headaches are normal; do not ascend if symptoms worsen; descend is the only treatment for AMS.

days.title: Point Lenana at sunrise
activities: Leave at about 03:00 by headtorch for Point Lenana (4,985 m), arriving at sunrise
Descend via Simba Col to Mintos Hut (about 4,300 m), views of Lake Michaelson
days.transport: On foot with a licensed guide
days.geographicalHighlight: Summit views of Mount Kenya's glaciated peaks and, on clear days, over the Chogoria side
days.practical: Weather-dependent: the summit can be skipped if the group or the weather is not ready.

days.title: The Gorges Valley and the Chogoria side
activities: Walk along the Gorges Valley rim and past Hall Tarns toward Lake Ellis (about 3,500 m)
Photograph Lake Michaelson and the Temple formation
days.geographicalHighlight: Glacial valleys, tarns and the Gorges Valley
days.practical: The Chogoria side is quieter than Naro Moru; keep a margin for rain.

days.title: Down to Chogoria and the capital
activities: Walk or take the 4x4 pick-up to Chogoria Gate (about 3,000 m) and the road
Drive about 4-5 h to Nairobi via Embu and Thika
Hot shower and a proper dinner; sleep in Nairobi
days.transport: On foot, then private driver-guide vehicle
days.accommodation: Hotel or guesthouse in Nairobi (Karen or Westlands)
days.culturalHighlight: Nairobi's food scene: nyama choma and Swahili cooking
days.practical: Arrive in daylight; do not leave bags in the vehicle.

days.title: Cycling Hell's Gate and the Rift Valley
activities: Drive about 90 km to Lake Naivasha (about 1.5-2 h)
Cycle in Hell's Gate with a guide and walk Ol Njorowa Gorge
Evening boat trip on the lake; sleep at a lakeside campsite or cottage
days.accommodation: Lakeside cottage or campsite near Naivasha
days.culturalHighlight: Olkaria and the Maasai market near the gorge
days.geographicalHighlight: Volcanic cliffs, geothermal steam and a freshwater lake in the Rift Valley
days.practical: Flexible: after the trek this can become a rest morning and a shorter cycle.

days.title: Across the Rift to the Mara
activities: Drive via Narok to the Maasai Mara (about 260 km), 5-6 h
Afternoon game drive with the driver-guide
days.accommodation: Mid-range tented camp near Sekenani or Talek gate
days.culturalHighlight: Maasai pastoral landscapes along the road
days.geographicalHighlight: Savanna and acacia plains of the Mara, elevation 1,500-2,200 m
days.practical: Mara reserve fees are per 24 h; the Jan-Jun rate applies.

days.title: A full day of resident game
activities: Dawn and late afternoon game drives for lion, elephant, giraffe and buffalo
Visit a community-run Maasai enterprise and walk with a guide
days.geographicalHighlight: Grassland, the Talek and Mara rivers
days.practical: Rain showers start in March; keep a margin.

days.title: Dawn drive and return to Nairobi
activities: Dawn game drive, then drive back through Narok to Nairobi (about 270 km)
Overnight in Nairobi; repack for the coast
days.practical: Flexible alternative: fly Mara to Wilson (about 1 h) if the road is poor.

days.title: Flight to the Swahili coast
activities: Fly Nairobi to Lamu-Manda airport (about 2 h) and cross by boat to Lamu Island
Walk through the old town at dusk and eat at a Swahili restaurant
In Ramadan (about 8 Feb-9 Mar) dress modestly and eat discreetly by day
days.transport: Jambojet or Safarilink flight, then boat
days.accommodation: Guesthouse or restored Swahili house, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Lamu Old Town, UNESCO World Heritage site (2001), the oldest Swahili settlement in East Africa
days.geographicalHighlight: Island of coral stone, mangroves and dhows
days.practical: Do not travel to Lamu by road; fly both ways. Stay on the islands.

days.title: Dhow day on the channel
activities: Sail by dhow along the Lamu channel to Shela village and the dunes
Visit Lamu Museum, the fort and the donkey sanctuary on foot
Evening iftar or sunset on the waterfront
days.culturalHighlight: Swahili architecture, Islamic heritage, dhow-building tradition
days.geographicalHighlight: Mangrove channels and a long Indian Ocean beach
days.practical: Stay within the islands and use local boatmen recommended by the guesthouse.

days.title: Fly back to Nairobi and Paris
activities: Rest and repack in Nairobi, evening flight to Paris CDG
Keep two hours of margin for the connection
days.transport: Jambojet or Safarilink flight, then international flight
days.practical: Book the international flight at least 6 hours after the Lamu landing.

days.title: Arrival in Paris
activities: Land in Paris CDG in the morning

security.summary: The route stays out of every area under advice against travel in the UK, French and Dutch advisories, and Lamu and Manda islands are excepted or yellow (air access only). It is rated conditional because terrorism and kidnapping threats are significant nationally and acute on the Lamu side, an Ebola outbreak linked to the DRC is only just ending, curfews apply in parts of Laikipia and Samburu next to the Mount Kenya approach, and pre-election unrest is expected from mid-2027.
security.assessedRoute: Nairobi - Nanyuki - Mount Kenya (Sirimon to Chogoria) - Nairobi - Naivasha/Hell's Gate - Maasai Mara (Narok County) - Nairobi - Lamu and Manda islands (air only) - Nairobi. Excluded from the route: Samburu, Buffalo Springs, Isiolo, Marsabit, Lamu mainland, Kiwayu, Garissa, Tana River, Malindi north, Moyale.

advisories.regionsAffected: Red: Mandera, Wajir, Garissa, mainland Lamu, Kiwayu. Orange: Marsabit, Moyale, Tana Delta and Malindi coast, parts of Mombasa and Nairobi slums.
advisories.routeImpact: Route avoids red and orange zones; herder-farmer violence in Laikipia and Samburu is flagged, so fly or use a guide on roads there.

conflictRisk.note: Armed conflict is confined to the Somali border counties and inter-communal violence in the north (Marsabit, Turkana, Samburu, Laikipia); none is on the route, but Laikipia curfews are close to the Nanyuki approach.

terrorismRisk.note: UK rates the threat high and France significant (Al Shabaab, some Daesh support); attacks have hit Nairobi (2019) and Manda Bay (2020). Official advice allows the route but crowded public places and hotels are potential targets.

kidnappingRisk.note: UK flags a high terrorist kidnapping threat in the northern border and coastal counties; the route stays out of them, and Lamu is by air only with local operators.

regionalRestrictions: Lamu and Manda islands: air access only; no road travel on the mainland of Lamu County.
Laikipia, Samburu, Baringo, Turkana, West Pokot and Elgeyo-Marakwet: curfews in some zones; limit movement (France).
Mount Kenya Sirimon gate lies at the edge of the Laikipia curfew counties; use a licensed operator and day-time transfers.
Ebola: Kenya's imported outbreak ended its last patient on 11 Nov 2026 and is in a 42-day countdown; the DRC outbreak continues.
ordinaryRisks: Violent crime, mugging and carjacking in Nairobi and on highways; fake police checkpoints; avoid night driving.
Road safety: poor driving standards and overloaded matatus; avoid long-distance buses.
Altitude sickness on Mount Kenya (4,985 m) with a fast ascent profile.
Wildlife: do not walk outside the permitted areas or swim in park rivers and lakes.
Malaria and dengue; flash floods and landslides in the Oct-Dec rains are over by February but roads can be damaged.
security.medicalAccess: Good private hospitals in Nairobi (Nairobi Hospital, Aga Khan); limited care on the mountain, in the Mara and on Lamu. Medical evacuation by air from the Mara and Lamu is possible but must be insured; Mount Kenya rescue relies on KWS and operators.
security.insuranceConsiderations: The state-run mandatory Kenyan health insurance is separate from a private policy; the private policy must cover trekking above 4,000 m, evacuation and ideally epidemic disruption. Check Ebola exclusions.
security.reassessmentRequired: Recheck France Diplomatie, UK FCDO and Dutch advice before booking and again two weeks before departure; reassess after the Ebola 42-day countdown ends (around late December 2026), and monitor pre-election tension and any Lamu incident. US State Department and Smartraveller pages could not be read in this check.

practicalRequirements.visa: Kenya eTA, USD 30 normal processing (about 72 h), expedited adds USD 100; apply at least two weeks ahead. French passport holders need an eTA; confirm on the official portal. From 5 October 2026 most visitors must also buy Kenyan government-provided health insurance during the application (about USD 44, secondary source).
practicalRequirements.entry: eTA approval printout, return ticket, accommodation details; Ebola screening on arrival from Uganda, Ethiopia and the DRC.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages.
permits: KWS park fees for Mount Kenya, Hell's Gate and the Mara (per day)
Licensed guide required for Mount Kenya high routes (operator-arranged)
practicalRequirements.insurance: Private insurance covering trekking to 5,000 m, medical evacuation and ideally epidemic disruption; separate from the mandatory Kenyan insurance.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile data in towns; none on the mountain; patchy in the Mara.
practicalRequirements.payments: Mobile money (M-Pesa) and cards in towns; cash in Kenyan shillings for park fees, tips and Lamu; ATMs in Nairobi and Nanyuki.
practicalRequirements.medical: Malaria prophylaxis, yellow fever certificate only if arriving from risk countries, hepatitis A and typhoid, rabies advice; Diamox discussion for altitude. Good care in Nairobi, limited elsewhere.
equipment: Layered clothing and a warm sleeping bag for -5 C

advantages: Three distinct landscapes and cultures in one trip
Point Lenana is a genuine summit without technical skills
Mara in the dry season with fewer vehicles than July-October
Hell's Gate lets the group cycle among wildlife
Lamu is a UNESCO Swahili town reached only by air
disadvantages: Costs about 3,400 EUR per person, outside the 2,500 EUR budget
Fast ascent profile on Mount Kenya raises altitude-sickness risk
Terrorism and kidnapping threats are significant nationally and on Lamu
Self-drive is not recommended, so the group depends on a paid driver-guide
uncertainties: Ebola: Kenya's imported outbreak is in a 42-day countdown (to about late December 2026) while the DRC outbreak continues
The final KWS 2027 tariff and the Mara county fee; the official fee sheet could not be read
US State Department and Smartraveller pages could not be fetched in this check
Safarilink and Jambojet Nairobi-Lamu schedules and fares for February 2027 are unconfirmed
Whether the Kenyan mandatory health insurance adds cost beyond USD 44 or conflicts with private cover

claims: Advises against all travel to Mandera County, parts of Wajir and Garissa, and all of Lamu County except Lamu Island and Manda Island

Advises against all but essential travel to Garissa Town, Tana River County north of the river up to Saka, the coastal strip within 15 km of the coast between the Tana and Athi-Galana-Sabaki rivers, and Moyale

sources.title: Kenya travel advice: Safety and security
claims: Terrorism threat is high across Kenya, mainly Al Shabaab; travel to Lamu and Manda by air through Lamu airport, not by road
Violent crime and carjacking frequent in cities and on highways; avoid night driving; fake checkpoints
Protests common, especially in Nairobi, and can turn violent
Altitude sickness on Mount Kenya; check insurance covers planned activities
